answer: Locked-collateral nullifiers keep each deposit attached to a single seat. Before an identity can grade a radio signal log, test a cipher library, or schedule dawn cargo inspections, it locks 1,800 POA and publishes a nullifier computed from that locked note and a network salt. Any later registration that repeats the nullifier is refused by every node, and the coins stay frozen for 20 epochs. Eighty fakes must therefore immobilize 144,000 POA at the same time; transferring the coins to another wallet fails because the first nullifier remains on the public list and cannot be reused.
